coded.vl: Statutory minimum wage applies on the same terms as other workers
coded.n: National minimum wage (QAR 1,000 a month) applies to domestic workers, plus QAR 500 housing and QAR 300 food if not provided.

coded.vl: At least monthly payment, documented, with limits on deductions or in-kind pay
coded.n: Paid at the end of the month and no later than the third day of the next, by bank account or in cash against a signed receipt; recruitment costs may not be deducted.

coded.vl: Only a daily rest rule, or a longer limit than for other workers
coded.n: Law sets a 10-hour daily cap excluding breaks; the standard contract sets 8 normal hours plus up to 2 hours' overtime at 125 per cent.
coded.src: Law 15/2017 art. 12; Standard Unified Contract art. 4; ILO FAIRWAY factsheet (Dec. 2023)

coded.vl: At least 24 consecutive hours, not replaceable by pay at the employer's request
Equal to or longer than for other workers
coded.n: Three weeks' paid annual leave a year, and a return air ticket home every two years.

coded.fn: Keeping own identity and travel documents
coded.vl: General rule only, not specific to domestic workers or without a penalty
coded.n: Confiscating passports is an offence (fine up to QAR 25,000), but the employer may keep the passport with the worker's written consent.

coded.vl: Accommodation standards only; living in may be required
coded.n: Suitable accommodation and food; no specific occupational safety or accommodation standard for domestic workers.

coded.vl: Worker may change employer without the employer's consent
coded.n: Change of employer at any time without the employer's permission, with one or two months' notice through the ministry system (compensation capped at two months' wage during probation); no exit permit, 72 hours' notice before leaving the country.
coded.src: Law 21/2015 and Executive Regulations arts 7, 65; ILO FAIRWAY factsheet (Dec. 2023)

coded.vl: Worker may not be charged recruitment fees
coded.n: The standard contract places recruitment fees on the agency or employer and bars deductions from the worker.
coded.src: Law 15/2017; Standard Unified Contract; ILO FAIRWAY factsheet (Dec. 2023)

coded.vl: Agencies licensed and liable to the worker (refund, return costs or joint liability)
coded.n: Licensed offices; liability for return in the probation period.
Complaint-based, including the online Unified Platform for Complaints and Whistleblowers.

coded.vl: Courts or labor tribunals on the same terms as other workers, or fee-free
coded.n: Ministry conciliation, then the Labour Dispute Settlement Committee (decision within three weeks, appeal to the Appellate Court, no court fees); unpaid awards via the Workers' Support and Insurance Fund.
coded.src: Law 13/2017; Cabinet Decision 6/2018; Law 17/2018; ILO FAIRWAY factsheet (Dec. 2023)

coded.vl: Partial: medical care, injury cover or employer insurance only
coded.n: Employer-paid medical care for sickness or injury; up to two weeks' paid sick leave after three months; end-of-service gratuity of three weeks' pay a year; maternity not specified.
coded.src: Law 15/2017 art. 15; Standard Unified Contract; ILO FAIRWAY factsheet (Dec. 2023)

coded.fn: Protection from abuse, harassment and violence
coded.vl: General criminal or civil law only
coded.n: Two government shelters for trafficking victims; complaints to the National Committee to Combat Human Trafficking.
Worker committees are open to Qatari workers only; joint committees exist at enterprises with 30 or more workers, which does not fit household employment.
coded.src: Law 14/2004 art. 116, ch. 13; ILO FAIRWAY factsheet (Dec. 2023)

dec.n: Article 26 complaint concerning Qatar (Forced Labour and Labour Inspection Conventions)
dec.pe: Worker delegates at the ILO filed a complaint in 2014 about migrant workers in Qatar. In 2017 the ILO closed it when Qatar agreed a programme of labour reforms with the ILO.
dec.pi: Delegasi pekerja di ILO mengajukan pengaduan pada 2014 tentang pekerja migran di Qatar. Pada 2017 ILO menutupnya ketika Qatar menyepakati program reformasi ketenagakerjaan dengan ILO.

dec.ct: Labour Dispute Settlement Committee, Qatar (as reported)
dec.pe: Workers of a construction company in Qatar were not paid for months. About 100 who stayed won their cases at the new labour committees, but reports say the money had not been paid months later.
dec.pi: Pekerja sebuah perusahaan konstruksi di Qatar tidak digaji berbulan-bulan. Sekitar 100 orang yang bertahan memenangkan perkara di komite perburuhan yang baru, tetapi menurut laporan uangnya belum dibayar berbulan-bulan kemudian.
